selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests two genuinely distinct strategy axes for achieving dual-band performance (UV reflection 200-400 nm, SWIR transmission 800-1500 nm) with HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica within 30 layers. Route 1 tests whether a periodic quarter-wave Bragg reflector topology, tuned to the UV band center, can naturally provide the required spectral separation. Route 2 tests whether breaking periodicity and allowing all layer thicknesses to vary independently can better satisfy both bands simultaneously through aperiodic optimization. These axes are complementary: if Route 1 succeeds, it offers simpler manufacturing; if Route 2 succeeds, it demonstrates the value of non-periodic design. Literature L05 directly supports the HfO2/SiO2 material pair for UV-to-IR applications, L13 provides the physics basis for quarter-wave stack reflectors, and L01 motivates UV filter efficiency considerations. No route optimizes refractive indices (measured data only); all tune geometry.

routes.title: Periodic Quarter-Wave UV Bragg Reflector
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack centered at 300 nm will produce a photonic bandgap with high reflectance in 200-400 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 800-1500 nm due to the wavelength scaling of Bragg resonance.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high-reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength λ0 where each layer has optical thickness λ0/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than λ0 (here 800-1500 nm vs 300 nm), the stack becomes increasingly transparent as the optical thicknesses become sub-quarter-wave.
soft_objectives: Minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Quarter-wave thicknesses at 300 nm are manufacturable with standard deposition
HfO2/SiO2 pair has established deposition processes per L05
theory_basis: Bragg reflection condition for periodic multilayers
Photonic bandgap formation in quarter-wave stacks
expected_advantages: Simple periodic structure reduces optimization complexity
28 layers provides strong UV reflection with margin under 30-layer limit
known_risks: Periodic structure may create secondary reflection bands in SWIR
Quarter-wave at 300 nm may not optimally balance both bands
Fixed periodicity limits ability to fine-tune spectral edges
routes.execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer stack on fused_silica substrate with air incidence. Stack topology: 14 repeated pairs of hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) (28 layers total), starting with hfo2 adjacent to air. Initial layer thicknesses: hfo2 at 75 nm, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) at 125 nm (quarter-wave optical thickness at 300 nm center wavelength). Optimization variables: scale factor applied uniformly to all layer thicknesses (range 0.8-1.2), and individual thickness adjustments per layer type within ±20% of scaled baseline. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Wavelength bands: 200-400 nm (maximize reflectance), 800-1500 nm (maximize transmittance). Material refractive indices from measured datasets for hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos). Total layer count fixed at 28.

routes.title: Aperiodic Thickness-Optimized Dual-Band Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An aperiodic 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve superior dual-band performance compared to periodic designs by decoupling the UV reflection and SWIR transmission requirements.
routes.design_principle: Aperiodic multilayers break the strict wavelength scaling of periodic stacks, allowing independent control of spectral features. Needle optimization or gradient-based methods can find thickness distributions that maximize transmission in one band while maximizing reflection in another without the constraint of periodicity.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | fused_silica substrate
soft_objectives: Minimize thickness variation between adjacent layers for manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Aperiodic thicknesses may require more precise deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 compatibility established per L05 and L08
expected_advantages: Greater design freedom than periodic stacks
Can suppress secondary reflection bands in SWIR
May achieve better spectral edge sharpness between UV and SWIR bands
known_risks: Higher optimization complexity with 24 independent variables
Aperiodic designs may be more sensitive to thickness errors
L01 notes UV filter challenges including solarization effects
routes.execution_request_english: Design an aperiodic multilayer stack on fused_silica substrate with air incidence. Stack topology: 24 alternating layers starting with hfo2 adjacent to air, ending with SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) adjacent to substrate (12 hfo2 layers, 12 SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers). Initial thicknesses: all layers start at 100 nm as a neutral baseline. Optimization variables: all 24 individual layer thicknesses, each independently tunable from 30 nm to 200 nm. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Wavelength bands: 200-400 nm (maximize reflectance), 800-1500 nm (maximize transmittance). Material refractive indices from measured datasets for hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos). Total layer count fixed at 24.

research_influence: L05 directly supports both routes by demonstrating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer viability from UV to IR, justifying the material pair choice
L13 informs Route 1's periodic quarter-wave approach by explaining photonic bandgap formation in dielectric multilayers
L08 reinforces HfO2/SiO2 as a established high/low index pair for NIR applications, supporting the SWIR transmission objective
L01 influences Route 2's risk assessment by noting UV filter challenges including solarization, which informs the manufacturing considerations
L17 was considered for UV damage resistance but not cited as it focuses on laser damage rather than the spectral design problem
unresolved_decisions: Fused silica substrate name resolution: 'fused_silica' is not in guaranteed_names but is explicitly required by the problem statement; the registry must resolve this name or the route will be returned for repair
Incidence angle not specified in problem: both routes assume normal incidence (0 degrees) as a deliberate design hypothesis; if oblique incidence is required, routes would need revision
Polarization state not specified: both routes assume unpolarized light; if s- or p-polarization is required for the UAV application, this would affect the optimal thickness distribution
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If both routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.7 after full optimization, the fundamental constraint of 30 layers with HfO2/SiO2 may be insufficient for the dual-band requirement; recommend expanding the material palette or relaxing the layer count limit.

Reflectance in 200-400 nm band should exceed 90% with 14 pairs
Transmittance in 800-1500 nm band should exceed 85% if secondary bands do not overlap
If hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early and tightest_margin will decrease as optimization attempts to suppress SWIR reflection bands
